meta.name: Release and build
meta.about: How a HAX release goes out, in order: generated from the ubiquity-push script in webcomponents and the GitHub workflows in each repo. One build of every element is copied into every platform, both backends are kept identical, and a shared version tag sets off release notes, containers and SBOMs.

kindLabels.rel: the order of steps and what triggers what

rl_psucdn.desc: Penn State's copy of the HAX build, at both cdn/ and haxcms/ paths, which hax.psu.edu sites load from.

r0.desc: lerna publish sends every changed element to npm under @haxtheweb. It is the one step done by hand, because it needs a person to confirm versions.

r1.desc: yarn run ubiquity: one build of every element into build/, plus wc-registry.json (tag to file) and wc-registry-graph.json (what loads what), so any site can lazy-load any element.

r2.desc: PRAW is the source for HAX agent skills. The index is built and snapshotted into the site boilerplate and both deployment roots as .well-known/agent-skills.

r3.desc: The same build/, build.js, build-haxcms.js, wc-registry.json and version are copied into HAX11ty, haxcms-php, haxcms-nodejs, haxsite, HAXiam, the Penn State CDN, the waxam mirror and ELMS:LN.

r4.desc: The theme list from haxcms-elements is copied into both backends' coreConfig, so both offer the same themes.

r5.desc: Real outline-designer output is recaptured and replayed through both backends' saveOutline in a contract test, so the designer and the backends never drift.

r6.desc: haxcms-nodejs's site boilerplate and coreConfig are mirrored into haxcms-php, and the CLI gets wc-registry.json to validate tags.

r7.desc: The component gallery is rebuilt for CDN publishing; pull requests get a Vercel preview of it.

r8.desc: Every repo commits, takes the same version with commit-and-tag-version and pushes with its tag.

rl_notes.desc: On every version tag, GitHub Actions builds a source archive and SHA256SUMS and publishes a GitHub release with generated notes. Workflows: release-checksums.yml, release-notes.yml, release.yml.

rl_docker.desc: On every version tag, the Node.js and PHP platforms are published to the GitHub Container Registry (ghcr.io/haxtheweb/...), with latest following the newest release. Workflows: docker-publish.yml.

rl_sbom.desc: Every release gets an SBOM of its dependencies. Workflows: sbom.yml.

rl_npm.desc: The CLI and haxcms-nodejs publish to npm from npm run release: build, tag with commit-and-tag-version, push, publish.

rl_vercel.desc: Every webcomponents pull request deploys the component gallery to a Vercel preview, where changes are reviewed.

rl_build.desc: build.yml on webcomponents runs on every push to master and nightly: install, lint, stylelint, Prettier, the full test suite in Playwright, then the gallery.

rl_parity.desc: backend-parity.yml runs on both backends so the two stay identical.

rl_codeql.desc: CodeQL, dependency audits, license checks and OpenSSF Scorecard run on every repo.

tours.label: How a release goes out
tours.message: One script carries a HAX release from npm to every platform, then a tag sets off the automation.

scenes.caption: 1. Publish packages. lerna publish sends every changed element to npm under @haxtheweb. It is the one step done by hand, because it needs a person to confirm versions.
2. Ubiquity build. yarn run ubiquity: one build of every element into build/, plus wc-registry.json (tag to file) and wc-registry-graph.json (what loads what), so any site can lazy-load any element.
3. Agent skills index. PRAW is the source for HAX agent skills. The index is built and snapshotted into the site boilerplate and both deployment roots as .well-known/agent-skills.

4. Normalize every project. The same build/, build.js, build-haxcms.js, wc-registry.json and version are copied into HAX11ty, haxcms-php, haxcms-nodejs, haxsite, HAXiam, the Penn State CDN, the waxam mirror and ELMS:LN.
5. Sync themes.json. The theme list from haxcms-elements is copied into both backends' coreConfig, so both offer the same themes.
6. Outline designer contract. Real outline-designer output is recaptured and replayed through both backends' saveOutline in a contract test, so the designer and the backends never drift.
7. Node.js is the boilerplate. haxcms-nodejs's site boilerplate and coreConfig are mirrored into haxcms-php, and the CLI gets wc-registry.json to validate tags.
8. Rebuild the gallery. The component gallery is rebuilt for CDN publishing; pull requests get a Vercel preview of it.
9. Version and tag everything. Every repo commits, takes the same version with commit-and-tag-version and pushes with its tag.
When the tag lands: release notes, checksums, containers, SBOMs and npm.
What guards it: nightly builds, backend parity, CodeQL and scorecards.
